summary: The PyQt5 cockpit is a flat 2D admin panel with a small isometric tower diagram drawn by QGraphicsScene. It is a technical proof of native packaging — not a 3D graphics-first cockpit. The user has rejected it as the main visual path.
honest_observations: PyQt5 cockpit is QGraphicsView (2D scene graph) — not a 3D engine.
Tower is depth-cued but rendered as 2D rectangles with painted shadows.
No perspective camera. No orbit. No rotate. No real Z-buffer.
Tower occupies ~22% of window — most space is HUD tables and text panels.
Floor interiors are HTML-like text dumps in QTextEdit, not 3D rooms.
Workers are not rendered as 3D entities — they are integer counts on chips.
Lifts are 10x10 px squares — not 3D cars in shafts.
Screenshot proof captured a working UI, not visual delight.
health 30/30 measures wiring quality, NOT visual quality.
This is acceptable as an admin/diagnostic fallback. It is NOT acceptable as the main 3D cockpit.
